overview: The Medford High School Advisory Teams for Exterior/Interior Design and Sustainability/MEP Systems met to review project goals, architectural context, and technical strategies for the new school. The teams discussed material durability, LEED certification targets, and energy-efficient building systems ahead of the Preferred Schematic Report.

items.title: Project Progress and Cost Models
items.summary: Designers reviewed the project schedule targeting a Fall 2030 opening and presented 29 high-level cost models recently shared with the full Building Committee.

items.title: Medford Civic Architecture Context
items.summary: The team examined Medford's historical shipbuilding and brickmaking industries alongside existing civic buildings to determine how the new school can foster a sense of belonging and civic identity.

items.title: Exterior Material Selection
items.summary: Architects compared exterior materials such as brick, stone, and metal panels based on a 50 to 75-year lifespan, cost-effectiveness, and aesthetic connection to the Fells landscape.

items.title: Interior Design and Materials
items.summary: The discussion focused on neutral, timeless interior palettes that support flexibility, diversity, and student autonomy while ensuring durability and low maintenance.

items.title: Experiential Graphic Design
items.summary: The team explored using experiential graphics for wayfinding, honoring school history, and utilizing the building itself as a teaching tool for vocational programs.

items.title: LEED Certification and Energy Targets
items.summary: The Sustainability team confirmed the project will register under LEED v5, requiring at least Silver certification for MSBA reimbursement while targeting an Energy Use Intensity (EUI) between 25 and 35.

items.title: Mechanical and Electrical Systems
items.summary: Engineers presented all-electric HVAC options, including ground-source and air-source heat pumps, while emphasizing the need for reliable systems that facilities staff can maintain.

items.title: Renewable Energy and Resiliency
items.summary: The team reviewed requirements for rooftop solar PV arrays and discussed battery storage as a method for demand response and community resiliency during power outages.

items.title: Embodied Carbon and Mass Timber
items.summary: Architects explored reducing the building's carbon footprint through low-carbon concrete and the potential use of mass timber or hybrid structural systems.

items.title: Indoor Environmental Quality and Health
items.summary: The team discussed strategies for maximizing daylight, improving air quality, and vetting materials to avoid Red List chemicals.

items.title: Lifecycle Cost Analysis (LCCA)
items.summary: Project leaders outlined the 50-year lifecycle cost analysis required by the MSBA to evaluate the long-term financial impact of building systems versus initial installation costs.
